title: Daily Life & Conversations
subtitle: Talk about your routine, make plans and handle phone calls

lessons.title: Ma vie quotidienne
lessons.description: Describe your daily routine and say how often you do things.

blocks.heading: A day in your life
blocks.body: At A2 level you can connect the steps of your day into full sentences. Reflexive verbs (se réveiller, se préparer...) describe things you do to yourself, and time expressions glue the day together.

examples.french: Je me réveille à sept heures.
examples.english: I wake up at seven o'clock.

examples.french: Je me prépare en vingt minutes.
examples.english: I get ready in twenty minutes.

examples.french: Je quitte la maison à huit heures et quart.
examples.english: I leave the house at a quarter past eight.

examples.french: Je commence le travail à neuf heures.
examples.english: I start work at nine o'clock.

examples.french: Le soir, je me détends devant la télévision.
examples.english: In the evening, I relax in front of the TV.

examples.french: Je me couche vers vingt-trois heures.
examples.english: I go to bed around eleven p.m.

blocks.tip: "Vers" (around) makes times sound natural: "vers midi" = around noon.

blocks.heading: How often? Frequency adverbs
blocks.body: Frequency adverbs say how often something happens: toujours (always), souvent (often), parfois (sometimes), rarement (rarely), jamais (never). They usually come right after the conjugated verb.

examples.french: Je prends toujours un café le matin.
examples.english: I always have a coffee in the morning.

examples.french: Il arrive souvent en retard.
examples.english: He often arrives late.

examples.french: Nous faisons parfois les courses le samedi.
examples.english: We sometimes do the shopping on Saturdays.

examples.french: Elle va rarement au cinéma.
examples.english: She rarely goes to the cinema.

examples.french: Je ne mange jamais devant l'ordinateur.
examples.english: I never eat in front of the computer.

examples.french: D'habitude, je dîne à vingt heures.
examples.english: Usually, I have dinner at eight p.m.

blocks.tip: "D'habitude" and "en général" usually start the sentence: "D'habitude, je me lève tôt."

blocks.heading: Household chores
blocks.body: French uses "faire" for most chores: faire le ménage (to do the housework), faire la vaisselle (the dishes), faire la lessive (the laundry), faire les courses (the shopping).

examples.french: Je fais le ménage le week-end.
examples.english: I do the housework at the weekend.

examples.french: Mon frère fait la vaisselle après le dîner.
examples.english: My brother does the dishes after dinner.

examples.french: Elle fait la lessive une fois par semaine.
examples.english: She does the laundry once a week.

examples.french: Nous faisons les courses au supermarché.
examples.english: We do the shopping at the supermarket.

examples.french: Je cuisine tous les soirs.
examples.english: I cook every evening.

blocks.heading: Reflexive verbs in the present
blocks.body: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun that matches the subject: me, te, se, nous, vous, se. Before a vowel, me/te/se become m'/t'/s'. The pronoun always comes right before the verb.

examples.french: Je me lève à sept heures.
examples.english: I get up at seven.

examples.french: Tu te prépares vite !
examples.english: You get ready quickly!

examples.french: Elle s'habille dans sa chambre.
examples.english: She gets dressed in her room.

examples.french: Nous nous reposons le dimanche.
examples.english: We rest on Sundays.

examples.french: Ils se couchent tard.
examples.english: They go to bed late.

blocks.tip: In the negative, "ne" goes before the pronoun: "Je ne me lève pas tôt."

blocks.heading: Where does the frequency adverb go?
blocks.body: Short adverbs (toujours, souvent, rarement) go right AFTER the conjugated verb, not before it as in English. "Jamais" works with "ne": ne + verb + jamais. Longer expressions (d'habitude, en général, tous les jours) can start or end the sentence.

examples.french: Je bois souvent du thé.
examples.english: I often drink tea.

examples.french: Elle est toujours à l'heure.
examples.english: She is always on time.

examples.french: Nous ne sortons jamais le lundi.
examples.english: We never go out on Mondays.

examples.french: D'habitude, il rentre à dix-huit heures.
examples.english: Usually, he gets home at six p.m.

passages.title: La semaine de Camille
passages.french:
Camille est infirmière à Lyon.
D'habitude, elle se réveille à six heures et elle se prépare rapidement.
Elle prend toujours un thé et une tartine, puis elle quitte la maison à sept heures.
Elle commence le travail à huit heures et elle finit à seize heures.
Après le travail, elle fait parfois les courses au marché.
Le soir, elle cuisine et elle se détend devant une série.
Le samedi, elle fait le ménage et la lessive.
Le dimanche, elle ne travaille jamais : elle se promène au parc et elle fait la sieste.
passages.english:
Camille is a nurse in Lyon.
Usually, she wakes up at six and gets ready quickly.
She always has a tea and a slice of bread with butter, then she leaves the house at seven.
She starts work at eight and finishes at four p.m.
After work, she sometimes does the shopping at the market.
In the evening, she cooks and relaxes in front of a series.
On Saturdays, she does the housework and the laundry.
On Sundays, she never works: she goes for a walk in the park and takes a nap.

lessons.title: On se retrouve ?
lessons.description: Invite friends, suggest activities, and accept or decline politely.

blocks.heading: Inviting someone
blocks.body: To invite someone, French speakers often ask a simple question with "tu veux" (do you want) or use "ça te dit" (does that appeal to you). "On" + verb is a friendly way to suggest doing something together.

examples.french: Tu veux aller au cinéma ce soir ?
examples.english: Do you want to go to the cinema tonight?

examples.french: Ça te dit de prendre un verre ?
examples.english: Do you fancy having a drink?

examples.french: On se retrouve à quelle heure ?
examples.english: What time shall we meet?

examples.french: Je t'invite au restaurant samedi.
examples.english: I'm inviting you to the restaurant on Saturday.

examples.french: Vous êtes libres dimanche ?
examples.english: Are you free on Sunday?

blocks.tip: "On" is used instead of "nous" in everyday speech: "On va au parc ?" = Shall we go to the park?

blocks.heading: Saying yes with enthusiasm
blocks.body: A plain "oui" works, but French has warmer ways to accept: volontiers (gladly), avec plaisir (with pleasure), pourquoi pas (why not), bonne idée (good idea).

examples.french: Volontiers, j'adore le cinéma !
examples.english: Gladly, I love the cinema!

examples.french: Avec plaisir ! À quelle heure ?
examples.english: With pleasure! At what time?

examples.french: D'accord, on se retrouve devant le musée.
examples.english: OK, we'll meet in front of the museum.

examples.french: Pourquoi pas ? Je suis libre samedi.
examples.english: Why not? I'm free on Saturday.

examples.french: Bonne idée ! J'ai très envie de sortir.
examples.english: Good idea! I really feel like going out.

blocks.heading: Declining politely
blocks.body: To refuse without hurting feelings, apologise first, give a reason, and soften it with "malheureusement" (unfortunately) or "c'est dommage" (that's a pity). "Je suis pris(e)" means "I'm busy / I have plans".

examples.french: Désolé, je ne peux pas ce soir.
examples.english: Sorry, I can't tonight.

examples.french: Malheureusement, je suis prise samedi.
examples.english: Unfortunately, I have plans on Saturday.

examples.french: C'est dommage, je dois travailler.
examples.english: That's a pity, I have to work.

examples.french: Une autre fois, peut-être ?
examples.english: Another time, maybe?

examples.french: Merci pour l'invitation, mais je ne suis pas libre.
examples.english: Thanks for the invitation, but I'm not free.

blocks.tip: Always propose an alternative — "une autre fois ?" — to show you still want to meet.

blocks.heading: Vouloir, pouvoir, devoir + infinitive
blocks.body: These three irregular verbs are the engine of making plans. They are followed directly by an infinitive: je veux sortir (I want to go out), je peux venir (I can come), je dois travailler (I have to work).

examples.french: Je veux voir ce film.
examples.english: I want to see this film.

examples.french: Tu peux venir à dix-neuf heures ?
examples.english: Can you come at seven p.m.?

examples.french: Elle doit finir son travail avant.
examples.english: She has to finish her work first.

examples.french: Nous voulons organiser un pique-nique.
examples.english: We want to organise a picnic.

examples.french: Vous pouvez nous rejoindre plus tard.
examples.english: You can join us later.

blocks.tip: Key forms: je veux / tu veux / il veut ; je peux / tu peux / il peut ; je dois / tu dois / il doit.

blocks.heading: Suggesting with "on"
blocks.body: In spoken French, "on" replaces "nous" and takes the same verb form as il/elle. As a question, it becomes a friendly suggestion: "On va au cinéma ?" = Shall we go to the cinema?

lessons.title: Au téléphone
lessons.description: Handle phone calls in French: answer, ask for someone, and leave a message.

blocks.heading: Answering the phone
blocks.body: French phone calls start with "Allô ?" — used ONLY on the phone, never in person. To introduce yourself, say "C'est..." (It's...) or, more formally, "... à l'appareil" (... speaking).

examples.french: Allô ? Bonjour, c'est Julien.
examples.english: Hello? Hi, it's Julien.

examples.french: Allô, oui ?
examples.english: Hello, yes?

examples.french: Marie Dubois à l'appareil.
examples.english: Marie Dubois speaking.

examples.french: C'est de la part de qui ?
examples.english: Who is calling, please?

examples.french: Je vous le passe.
examples.english: I'll put him through to you.

blocks.tip: On a professional call, give your full name after "allô": "Allô, bonjour, Paul Martin à l'appareil."

blocks.heading: Asking for someone and leaving a message
blocks.body: To ask for someone, use "Est-ce que je peux parler à... ?" or "Je voudrais parler à...". If the person is not there, you can leave a message: "Est-ce que je peux laisser un message ?"

examples.french: Est-ce que je peux parler à Madame Roche ?
examples.english: May I speak to Mrs Roche?

examples.french: Je voudrais parler au directeur, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: I would like to speak to the director, please.

examples.french: Elle n'est pas là pour le moment.
examples.english: She is not here at the moment.

examples.french: Est-ce que je peux laisser un message ?
examples.english: Can I leave a message?

examples.french: Vous pouvez rappeler plus tard ?
examples.english: Can you call back later?

examples.french: Ne quittez pas, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: Hold the line, please.

blocks.heading: Phone problems and text messages
blocks.body: Bad connection? Useful phrases: "Je vous entends mal" (I can't hear you well), "Ça coupe" (it's breaking up), "Vous vous êtes trompé de numéro" (you have the wrong number). For texting, the French say "un texto" or "un SMS".

examples.french: Je t'entends très mal, je te rappelle.
examples.english: I can hear you very badly, I'll call you back.

examples.french: Désolé, vous vous êtes trompé de numéro.
examples.english: Sorry, you have the wrong number.

examples.french: Ma batterie est presque vide.
examples.english: My battery is almost dead.

examples.french: Envoie-moi un texto quand tu arrives.
examples.english: Send me a text when you arrive.

examples.french: Je t'ai laissé un message sur ton répondeur.
examples.english: I left you a message on your voicemail.

blocks.tip: "Portable" means mobile phone in France; in Québec you'll hear "cellulaire".

blocks.heading: Polite requests with "je voudrais" and "est-ce que je peux"
blocks.body: On the phone, soften your requests. "Je voudrais" (I would like) is more polite than "je veux". "Est-ce que je peux + infinitive" asks for permission: May I...?

examples.french: Je voudrais parler à Madame Roche, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: I would like to speak to Mrs Roche, please.

examples.french: Est-ce que je peux parler à Thomas ?
examples.english: May I speak to Thomas?

examples.french: Est-ce que je peux laisser un message ?
examples.english: May I leave a message?

examples.french: Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
examples.english: Can you repeat, please?

blocks.tip: "Je voudrais" is the conditional of "vouloir" — you'll meet the full conditional at B1.

blocks.heading: Object pronouns you hear on the phone
blocks.body: Phone French is full of little pronouns before the verb: le/la (him/her), lui (to him/to her), vous (to you). You don't need to master them yet — just recognise the classic phrases.

passages.title: Un appel au bureau
passages.french:
La secrétaire : Cabinet Morel, bonjour !
M. Lambert : Bonjour, madame. Je voudrais parler à Madame Morel, s'il vous plaît.
La secrétaire : C'est de la part de qui ?
M. Lambert : De Monsieur Lambert, de la société Technova.
La secrétaire : Ne quittez pas, je vous la passe... Je suis désolée, elle est en réunion.
M. Lambert : Est-ce que je peux laisser un message ?
La secrétaire : Bien sûr, monsieur.
M. Lambert : Elle peut me rappeler au zéro six, quarante-cinq, vingt-deux ? C'est assez urgent.
La secrétaire : C'est noté, Monsieur Lambert. Bonne journée !
passages.english:
The secretary: Morel office, hello!
Mr Lambert: Hello, ma'am. I would like to speak to Mrs Morel, please.
The secretary: Who is calling?
Mr Lambert: Mr Lambert, from the company Technova.
The secretary: Hold the line, I'll put her through... I'm sorry, she is in a meeting.
Mr Lambert: May I leave a message?
The secretary: Of course, sir.
Mr Lambert: Can she call me back on oh six, forty-five, twenty-two? It's quite urgent.
The secretary: Noted, Mr Lambert. Have a good day!
